 Jalen Johnson had 12 points (4-of-12 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), nine rebounds, 11 assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s game against the Heat. 
 Johnson was just one rebound shy of a triple-double. While that makes for a somewhat solid stat line, he also shot 4-of-12 from the field and was -23 in 36 minutes in a 12-point loss at home to the Heat, who entered play Wednesday winless. It’ll be a quick turnaround for Johnson as the Hawks take on the Cavaliers at home Thursday. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Jalen Johnson led the Hawks with 21 points (5-of-14 FGs, 10-of-12 FTs), nine rebounds, four assists, two steals, two blocks and one three-pointer in a 120-110 loss to the Rockets on Monday. 
 It wasn’t as dominant of a performance as he put together against Houston on Saturday, but Johnson was still able to provide value across the board in the rematch. However, that didn’t change the result on the scoreboard. Johnson will continue to stuff the stat sheet for Atlanta, which has allowed him to be one of the best players in fantasy basketball so far this season despite a rough start shooting the ball. 
 Jalen Johnson 
 ATL 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Jalen Johnson led the Hawks with 26 points (8-of-19 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), nine rebounds, 16 assists, two steals and two three-pointers in a 121-114 loss to the Rockets on Saturday. 
 The Hawks dropped a game for the first time this season, but Johnson was still fantastic for fantasy managers. His field goal percentage was subpar, but the near triple-double made up for it, especially since he matched his career high for assists. Johnson’s shooting percentage has been rough in two of Atlanta’s three games so far, but he is currently averaging a triple-double, which has allowed him to be one of the best players in fantasy basketball to this point. 
 Jalen Johnson 
 ATL 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Jalen Johnson had 19 points (9-of-16 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), seven rebounds, eight assists, three steals and one block in Friday’s game against the Hornets. 
 With less than two minutes left in the first half, Dyson Daniel hit the floor for one of his seven steals, leading to a Jalen Johnson alley-oop dunk on the other end. That pretty much encapsulates how the night went for the Hawks as Johnson led the team in scoring with 19 in the 128-81 blowout win. Johnson showed he was able to move past the extracurriculars with the Magic on Wednesday with his usual excellent performance against the Hornets. 
 Jalen Johnson 
 ATL 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Jalen Johnson had 20 points (7-of-19 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), 14 rebounds and six assists against the Magic on Wednesday. 
 Double-doubles are nothing new for Johnson as the 24-year-old forward has averaged at least 10 rebounds in each of the last two seasons. He pulled down 14 rebounds Wednesday against the Magic and scored 20 points for his first double-double of the season. Johnson was involved in a play where he appeared to crash into Magic guard Desmond Bane with his elbow and later had to be separated from Paolo Banchero, who was presumably letting him hear about it on the court after the game. 
 Jalen Johnson 
 ATL 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Jalen Johnson tallied 20 points (8-of-12 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists and two three-pointers in Saturday’s exhibition against the Pacers. 
 Johnson had a productive night in Indy, leading all scorers with 20 points and shooting efficiently from the field. Coming off his best season to date, the Hawks forward has a Top-10 ADP in Yahoo! category leagues. Even if Johnson doesn’t meet those lofty expectations, his skill set is strong enough to still provide excellent fantasy value this season. 
 Luguentz Dort 
 ATL 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Luguentz Dort (knee) and Jalen Johnson (rest) are out for Thursday’s game against the Spurs 
 While Johnson is getting the night off to rest, Dort’s unofficial Hawks debut has been delayed due to a left knee contusion. Acquired from the Thunder during the offseason, Dort is expected to provide defense and physicality on the wing. He wasn’t a reliable fantasy option in Oklahoma City, and that’s unlikely to change in Atlanta. 
 Jalen Johnson 
 ATL 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Jalen Johnson amassed eight points (1-of-7 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, three assists and one steal across 17 minutes in Monday’s preseason loss to the Grizzlies. 
 Johnson will be the focal point of Atlanta’s franchise until further notice, which gives him a chance to finish as one of the more impactful all-around contributors in the fantasy landscape. The 24-year-old rising star will come off the board towards the end of the first round in nearly all fantasy drafts after averaging 22.5 points, 10.3 rebounds and 7.9 assists last year. 
 Jalen Duren 
 DET 
 Center 
 #0 
 Jalen Duren, Chet Holmgren, Jalen Johnson, Tyrese Maxey and Jamal Murray were named third-team All-NBA on Sunday. 
 All five third-team selections were named All-NBA for the first time in their respective careers on Sunday. Duren’s selection may be the most impactful, as he’ll hit restricted free agency next month. The All-NBA selection makes him eligible for a max deal worth up to $287 million over five years. However, given his struggles during the postseason and the Pistons’ need to also address Ausar Thompson’s future, Duren may not strike it that rich this summer. Especially with other teams unable to offer a deal on par with what the Pistons can. 
 Jalen Johnson 
 ATL 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Jalen Johnson finished Thursday’s loss to the Knicks with 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), eight rebounds, six assists, one block and two three-pointers. 
 Johnson was Atlanta’s best scorer on Thursday. In 32 minutes, he was the only player on the Hawks to reach the 20-point mark, which he did by using a combination of two-point scoring, three-point efficiency, and free-throw production. He also led the team in rebounds and assists before the final horn sounded. Johnson took a major leap in production this season and averaged 22.5 points, 10.3 rebounds and 7.9 assists over 72 regular-season games, while becoming an NBA All-Star for the first time. Another leap in Year 6 would bring even more fantasy value. 
 Jalen Johnson 
 ATL 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Jalen Johnson recorded a double-double on Tuesday with 18 points (7-of-15 FGs), 10 rebounds, six assists, two steals and one three-pointer in a 126-97 loss to the Knicks in Game 5. 
 Johnson struggled mightily in Game 4 on Saturday, and while he was more effective in this one, it wasn’t enough to get the Hawks on the right side of the scoreboard. He was better, but he hasn’t played to the level that Atlanta needs their All-Star to play at. He’ll need to make more of an impact on both ends of the floor in Game 6 on Thursday for the Hawks to avoid elimination.

 James Harden led the Cavaliers with 24 points (7-of-14 FGs), five rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in a 114-111 loss to the Hawks on Thursday.
 Harden has been underwhelming this season, with his scoring, assists and shooting efficiency all down. However, he was able to get his shot going in this one, and he ended up scoring at least 20 points for the first time this season while also having his best field goal percentage of the season. However, the trade-off was a new season low for assists. Harden should be better as the season progresses, but he may not play to his third-round ADP.
